title: Carbon — Allotropes and Carbon Monoxide
notes: **Crystalline allotropes:** diamond (each C sp3 tetrahedral, hardest natural substance, insulator, high refractive index), graphite (sp2 hexagonal layers, conductor along layers, lubricant), graphene (single layer of graphite, exceptional strength and conductivity).
**Amorphous allotropes:** charcoal (activated charcoal adsorbs gases), coke (fuel in blast furnaces), lamp black (pigment and filler in inks and tyres).
**Fullerenes:** $C_{60}$ (buckminsterfullerene, football shape), $C_{70}$, nanotubes. Discovered 1985. Spherical or tubular carbon molecules with unique electronic and mechanical properties.

**Carbon monoxide:** formed by incomplete combustion. Reducing agent: $Fe_2O_3 + 3CO \rightarrow 2Fe + 3CO_2$. Toxic because it binds haemoglobin 210 times more strongly than oxygen, causing asphyxiation.
**Uses of CO:** reducing agent in metallurgy, component of water gas ($CO + H_2$), feedstock for methanol and acetic acid synthesis.
